latest.content:

Upland Resources Limited
("Upland", the "Company" or the "Group")
LSOG Phase Two Underway as Drilling Commences in Wyoming
Upland Resources Limited (LSE: UPL.L; OTCQB: UPLLF) is pleased to provide an update on the commencement of Phase Two of Lost Soldier Oil and Gas' ("LSOG") development programme ("Phase Two") in the Green River Basin, Wyoming, United States, through the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, Upland Resources (Wyoming) Ltd.
GMF-5 Well - Deep Drilling:
• Phase Two of the LSOG development programme has started with the third well,
GMF-5
, spudded on 18th September 2026. Drilling and well operations are expected to take approximately 60 days.
• LSOG's current estimates from phase one that included two drills indicate potential resources of up to 5-6 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of gas across multiple stacked natural gas formations.
• This third GMF-5 well is planned to drill to approximately 19,000 feet (c. 5,800 metres), targeting a new overpressured zone beneath formations identified from the first two wells in phase one.
• This third well is intended to provide further information on the deeper resource potential, with an opportunity to advance understanding of the Niobrara and Frontier formations, which represent important deep, high-pressure targets within the project.
Production Update:
• LSOG has outlined plans to connect three wells to the pipeline being built this year, with production expected before year-end, subject to the successful completion of the required development and operational activities.
• On-site development activity is progressing, with surveying underway, pipeline preparations advancing and additional infrastructure being installed to support the growing operational programme.
Upland views these developments as an important step in the transition of the LSOG project from geological and resource evaluation towards commercial development and production.
The Company will provide further updates on the progress of the GMF-5 well and Phase Two as appropriate.
Upland's Strategic Relationship with LSOG
• Upland has invested approximately
US$4.3 million
to date in LSOG, held through its wholly owned subsidiary, Upland Resources (Wyoming) Ltd, and holds a further
US$9.5 million
of options in LSOG Class C units, with the option period remaining in place until 31st December 2030, giving total existing and potential exposure of US$13.8 million, totalling approximately 5% of the private placement.
• LSOG holds approximately a
6%
position in Upland, creating a strong alignment of interests between the two companies.
• Upland's Class C units carry a royalty interest on all production from the Wild Mustang Federal Unit leases, with no exposure to well costs or operating liabilities. Therefore, any additional volumes discovered through Phase Two, subject to commercial production, would benefit Upland at no further cost.
The relationship between Upland and LSOG extends beyond Upland's investment in the Wild Mustang project and forms an important part of Upland's broader international growth strategy.
The strategic relationship also encompasses the
US$100 million Strategic Funding Commitment
secured from Wild Mustang Midstream LLC, a subsidiary of LSOG, in respect of targeted upstream opportunities across Southeast Asia between 2026 and 2030.
Under the commitment, funding is intended to be deployed through asset-level farm-in arrangements, whereby LSOG may participate in specific licences by funding agreed exploration, appraisal and development work programmes. This provides Upland with a potential route to progress targeted licences while leveraging LSOG's capital, technical expertise and operational capabilities.
This update builds on the
Framework Agreement
announced on 24th November 2025, the
US$100 million Strategic Funding Commitment
announced on 23rd January 2026 and the
Bilateral Options Agreement
announced on 6th March 2026.
US$100m Strategic Funding Commitment - Upland
Bilateral Agreement - Lost Soldier Oil and Gas - Upland
Southeast Asia
The Company is pleased to report that progress across its Southeast Asian portfolio is advancing rapidly, with a number of asset-level developments progressing towards key milestones. Upland looks forward to updating shareholders on these developments as they become appropriate for announcement.
Management Commentary
Datuk Bolhassan Di, Chairman and CEO of Upland Resources Limited, commented:
"We are very pleased to see Phase Two of the LSOG development programme now underway with the spudding of GMF-5, marking the first test of the deeper section beneath the Wild Mustang Federal Unit.
This is an important milestone for LSOG and comes at a time when Upland continues to make significant progress across its core Southeast Asian portfolio. Our focus remains firmly on advancing these opportunities, which are progressing rapidly, and we look forward to providing further updates to the market as appropriate.
Our investment in LSOG reflects our confidence in the potential of the Green River Basin and the strength of the strategic relationship we have developed with the LSOG team. Importantly, through our Class C units, Upland participates in any discovery made by GMF-5 without contributing to the cost of drilling the well.
We look forward to the results of GMF-5, the continued advancement of Phase Two and LSOG's progress towards first production, alongside further developments across Upland's Southeast Asian portfolio."

company_30s.what_they_do: UPL Ltd. makes specialty chemicals that help farmers grow crops, and it also supplies industrial chemicals used in plastics, paints and other products. Think of it as a supplier of the ingredients that make seeds, fertilizers and industrial coatings work better.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company operates in a world where food security and industrial growth are key. Its products touch billions of acres of farmland and the manufacturing of everyday goods, giving it a built‑in demand that is hard to replace.
company_30s.current_state: UPL is in a restructuring phase, trying to trim costs while focusing on its core markets. Cash is being conserved and the company is looking for new investment or strategic deals to keep operations going. The share price is trading well below the level that many analysts would consider fair for the business’s fundamentals.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy with corporate governance moves – new directors, share placements and an annual report that shows it is still trying to balance its books.
Operationally, UPL has released a drilling and production report that hints at some progress in its Southeast Asian fields, and it is pursuing opportunities in Borneo and Sumatra.

On the regulatory side, the firm has gained approval to trade on the OTCQB venture market and has secured a strategic investment from a U.S. investor group, which could provide a fresh cash injection.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Cautiously optimistic – people are watching for a clear sign that the company’s operations are turning around.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the company’s cash reserves, the new U.S. investment, and the expectation that an upcoming award announcement will lift the stock.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the market has not yet responded to the operational updates and that any stop‑losses triggered by a weak rally could send the price lower again.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has shifted from vague speculation to a focus on the next drilling report and the potential award. If those pieces of news arrive, the mood could swing sharply.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no recent search interest. This lack of public attention means a surprise catalyst could hit the price with a big move.

near_term_catalysts: The next drilling and production report due in late September could confirm that the company’s field development is progressing, giving a clear positive signal to investors.
An award or royalty announcement from a partner in Southeast Asia would provide a concrete cash boost.
The scheduled approval to trade on the OTCQB could increase liquidity and attract new buyers.
If the U.S. investor group follows through on its commitment, the resulting capital injection could be the spark needed for a recovery.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in trading volume that coincides with the release of any of the above reports, a price break above the recent 20‑day moving average, or a clear statement from management about a new partnership or funding round.
expect_next.timing_regime: The share is still in the early stages of its crash‑recovery cycle. It has not yet shown a firm bottom, so we need a clear confirmation from one of the catalysts before we can expect a sustained rebound.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company’s operational updates prove credible, the price could climb to a level that is roughly halfway to its all‑time high. Historically, a deep bottom that falls 70‑95% can double or triple before returning to a more normal range. With the stock trading at a steep discount, a 200‑250% upside is realistic if the next catalyst triggers a bounce.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is that the operational reports show little progress, or that the new investor falls through. In that scenario the share could stay in the 70‑80% drop zone for months, and a weak rebound could be followed by another wipe‑out. A worst‑case scenario would leave the share near its current price, offering only a small return after transaction costs.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is limited to the current price (the worst case is a flat or slightly lower price). Potential gain could be 2.5–3× the entry price if the company delivers on its operational promises. The asymmetry is clear: the upside far outweighs the downside.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a volume spike that confirms the release of a positive report. Size the position so that a 10‑15% pullback does not wipe out the trade. Place a stop just below the most recent swing low – about 5–7% below the entry to protect against a false break.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash or a small position until you see a clear announcement of an award, new funding, or a sharp uptick in volume. Watch the 20‑day moving average; a break above it with high volume is a good entry signal.
playbook.if_passing: No immediate terminal risk is visible, so the default stance remains bullish. If the company were to be delisted or file for bankruptcy, that would be the only reason to abandon the play.

ai_insights.bottom_line: The share is deeply out of line with its fundamentals, the market has largely ignored it, and a clear operational or funding announcement could trigger a strong rebound – a classic contrarian setup.
